Project root is the cwd. "Heard" is a two-sided marketplace (customers pay to talk with companion
listeners who are all blind/visually impaired; non-clinical, never therapy; accessibility is the
product). Stack: Next.js 16 App Router, TS strict, Supabase (Postgres+Auth+Storage), Tailwind v4,
Zod, Vitest/RTL/jest-axe, Playwright. Mock mode (INTEGRATIONS_MODE=mock) via adapters in
lib/integrations/*. Money is integer cents in lib/pricing.ts. The MVP (M0–M9) and the
Listener/Customer/Admin dashboards (M10–M14) are all built and merged to main.

Governing docs at repo root: SPEC.md, BUILD_PLAN.md, DASHBOARDS_BUILD_PLAN.md,
DASHBOARDS_REQUIREMENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, README.md. READ the docs relevant to your dimension AND the
actual code (use Read/Grep/Glob). Report only REAL, grounded gaps — things actually missing,
partial, risky, or debt — not hypotheticals. For each, give a concrete file/doc pointer and a
specific recommendation. Be exhaustive within your dimension; it's fine to return many findings.

DIMENSION: Accessibility (the product's whole point — WCAG 2.2 AA floor, AAA body). Read components/ui/*, the session/call screens (app/(customer)/session/**, app/(provider)/provider/session/**), Dialog, forms, and SPEC.md §10. Beyond the M14 dashboard pass, find remaining gaps: the app-wide <Link><Button> nested-interactive (<a><button>) pattern, reduced-motion handling, 200% zoom/reflow, focus order + focus trap in Dialog, live-region coverage on the live call (timer/captions/mute), form error association, skip-link correctness, and any icon-only controls. Verify contrast claims against the real @theme tokens in app/globals.css — do not guess ratios.

1	# Build Specification — "Heard" (working name)
2	
3	> A two-sided marketplace where people pay to talk with, and be listened to by, professional **companion listeners — all of whom are legally blind or visually impaired.** Non-clinical companionship and conversation. US market, English (i18n-ready).
4	
5	**This document is the full build spec for Claude Code.** Read it together with `CLAUDE.md` (conventions Claude Code must follow) and `BUILD_PLAN.md` (the phased milestone plan). The UI/UX is specified separately in `../Interactive_Prototype_Design_Brief.md` — follow it for screens, components, palette, and accessibility detail.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 1. Decisions locked for this build
10	
11	| Decision | Choice |
12	|---|---|
13	| Build approach | **App-first.** Build the whole app end-to-end now; Stripe, Zoom, and Checkr are **mocked behind adapters** and swapped for real later. |
14	| Stack | **Next.js (App Router) + TypeScript + Supabase + Tailwind CSS.** Deploy target Vercel + Supabase. |
15	| Pricing | **Hybrid:** fixed blocks of **15 / 30 / 45 min** at a set price, plus **per-minute overage** if the call runs past the block. |
16	| Commission | **5%** platform fee (provider keeps 95%). Stored as config (`PLATFORM_COMMISSION_RATE`), never hard-coded. |
17	| Payouts | Weekly (mocked). |
18	| Auth | **Email + password** (Supabase Auth). Roles: `customer`, `provider`, `admin`. |
19	| Languages | **English only**, but i18n-ready (all copy via message catalog). |
20	| Admin scope | **Provider approval only** (approve/reject/suspend). Reporting & moderation UI are **deferred** (see §12). |
21	| Accessibility | **WCAG 2.2 AA minimum**, AAA contrast on body text. Non-negotiable. |
22	
23	> **Honest note carried into the build:** at 5% commission, per-session margin is thin after payment fees. `lib/pricing.ts` centralizes the rate so it is trivial to change, and the schema supports tips and (future) subscriptions as additional revenue.
24	
25	---
26	
27	## 2. Product overview
28	
29	Customers arrive lonely or wanting company. They discover a listener by hearing a short **voice intro**, book a **session block**, and have an audio conversation. Providers are blind/visually-impaired adults working from home by screen reader; the product exists to give them dignified, flexible income. The whole experience must be calm, warm, trustworthy, and operable entirely by keyboard and screen reader.
30	
31	**Core promise to reflect everywhere:** companionship, *not therapy*. A persistent, gentle "companionship, not medical or mental-health care — if you're in crisis, find support" affordance appears on every screen.
32	
33	---
34	
35	## 3. Architecture
36	
37	### 3.1 High level
38	- **Next.js App Router** app on Vercel. React Server Components + Server Actions for data work; client components only for interactive UI.
39	- **Supabase** for Postgres, Auth (email+password), and Storage (voice intros, avatars). **Row-Level Security on every table.**
40	- **Route handlers** (`app/api/**`) for webhooks (used by the *real* adapters later) and any server endpoints.
41	- **Zod** validates every input at the boundary (server actions, route handlers).
42	- All external services (**payments, calls, background checks**) are reached **only** through adapter interfaces — never called directly from feature code.
43	
44	### 3.2 The adapter pattern (the most important rule)
45	
46	Each external concern has: an **interface**, a **mock implementation** (default, used in this build), a **real implementation** (stubbed with `// TODO: real integration` for later), and an **`index.ts`** that selects one based on `INTEGRATIONS_MODE` (`mock` | `real`).
47	
48	```
49	lib/integrations/
50	  payments/        interface.ts  mock.ts  real.ts  index.ts
51	  calls/           interface.ts  mock.ts  real.ts  index.ts
52	  background-check/ interface.ts  mock.ts  real.ts  index.ts
53	```
54	
55	**PaymentsProvider** (maps to Stripe Connect later)
56	```ts
57	interface PaymentsProvider {
58	  ensureCustomer(userId: string): Promise<{ customerRef: string }>;
59	  authorizeHold(p: { bookingId: string; amountCents: number; customerRef: string }): Promise<{ paymentRef: string; status: "authorized" }>;
60	  capture(p: { paymentRef: string; amountCents: number }): Promise<{ status: "captured" }>;
61	  refund(p: { paymentRef: string; amountCents: number }): Promise<{ status: "refunded" }>;
62	  ensureConnectedAccount(providerId: string): Promise<{ accountRef: string }>;
63	  recordProviderEarning(p: { providerId: string; amountCents: number; sessionId: string }): Promise<void>;
64	  runWeeklyPayouts(): Promise<{ payouts: Array<{ providerId: string; amountCents: number }> }>;
65	}
66	```
67	*Mock:* writes an in-DB ledger (`payments`, `payouts`) and returns synthetic refs (`mock_pay_…`). No money moves.
68	
69	**CallProvider** (maps to Zoom Meeting SDK later)
70	```ts
71	interface CallProvider {
72	  createSession(p: { bookingId: string; providerId: string; customerId: string; maxMinutes: number }): Promise<{ callSessionRef: string }>;
73	  getJoinInfo(p: { callSessionRef: string; role: "host" | "participant"; userId: string }): Promise<{ joinRef: string; mockMode: boolean }>;
74	  endSession(p: { callSessionRef: string }): Promise<{ endedAt: string }>;
75	}
76	```
77	*Mock:* returns synthetic refs; the UI renders the **in-app mock call screen** (avatar + waveform, count-up timer, mute, captions, end). No real audio. The timer is the source of truth for elapsed time in mock mode.
78	
79	**BackgroundCheckProvider** (maps to Checkr later)
80	```ts
81	interface BackgroundCheckProvider {
82	  initiate(p: { providerId: string }): Promise<{ checkRef: string; status: "pending" }>;
83	  getStatus(p: { checkRef: string }): Promise<{ status: "pending" | "clear" | "consider" }>;
84	}
85	```
86	*Mock:* returns `pending`; an **admin** clears the provider manually (stands in for Checkr).
87	
88	> **Rule:** feature code imports `getPayments()`, `getCalls()`, `getBackgroundCheck()` from the integration `index.ts`. It must never import `mock.ts`/`real.ts` directly, and never reference Stripe/Zoom/Checkr SDKs outside `real.ts`.
89	
90	---
91	
92	## 4. Data model (Postgres / Supabase)
93	
94	Money is always **integer cents**. Timestamps are `timestamptz`. All tables have `id uuid default gen_random_uuid()`, `created_at`, `updated_at`. Define as SQL migrations in `supabase/migrations/` with **RLS policies** and a `supabase/seed.sql`.
95	
96	| Table | Key columns | Notes |
97	|---|---|---|
98	| `profiles` | `id` (FK `auth.users`), `role` (`customer`/`provider`/`admin`), `full_name`, `email`, `locale` | One row per user, created on sign-up. |
99	| `providers` | `id` (FK `profiles`), `display_name`, `bio`, `voice_intro_path`, `avatar_color`, `status` (`pending`/`approved`/`rejected`/`suspended`), `languages text[]`, `topics text[]`, `price_block_15_cents`, `price_block_30_cents`, `price_block_45_cents`, `overage_per_min_cents`, `is_available_now bool`, `rating_avg numeric`, `rating_count int`, `bg_check_ref`, `bg_check_status`, `payout_account_ref` | Provider profile + economics. |
100	| `availability_slots` | `provider_id`, `start_at`, `end_at`, `is_booked bool` | For scheduled bookings (optional in MVP alongside "now"). |
101	| `bookings` | `customer_id`, `provider_id`, `slot_id` (nullable), `block_minutes` (15/30/45), `start_mode` (`now`/`scheduled`), `scheduled_at`, `price_block_cents`, `overage_per_min_cents`, `status` (`pending`/`confirmed`/`in_progress`/`completed`/`cancelled`), `payment_ref` | A purchase intent. |
102	| `sessions` | `booking_id`, `provider_id`, `customer_id`, `call_session_ref`, `started_at`, `ended_at`, `elapsed_seconds`, `block_minutes`, `overage_minutes`, `total_price_cents`, `commission_cents`, `provider_earnings_cents`, `status` | The actual call + final accounting. |
103	| `payments` | `booking_id`, `customer_id`, `amount_cents`, `status` (`authorized`/`captured`/`refunded`/`failed`), `payment_ref` | Ledger row per booking. |
104	| `payouts` | `provider_id`, `period_start`, `period_end`, `amount_cents`, `status` (`scheduled`/`paid`), `scheduled_for` | Weekly aggregation (mock). |
105	| `reviews` | `session_id`, `customer_id`, `provider_id`, `rating` (1–5), `comment`, `tip_cents` | Updates provider rating; tip adds to earnings. |
106	| `reports` | `reporter_id`, `target_id`, `session_id`, `reason`, `status` (`open`/`reviewed`) | **Table only** for now (records in-app reports); moderation UI deferred (§12). |
107	
108	**RLS summary:** customers read/write only their own `bookings`/`sessions`/`payments`/`reviews`; providers read their own `providers`/`sessions`/`payouts`; **public** reads only the public fields of `approved` providers; `admin` role reads/writes all. Privileged server actions use the Supabase service-role client.
109	
110	---
111	
112	## 5. Pricing & accounting logic (`lib/pricing.ts`)
113	
114	Single source of truth. Pure, unit-tested functions. No pricing math anywhere else.
115	
116	```ts
117	const COMMISSION = Number(process.env.PLATFORM_COMMISSION_RATE ?? "0.05");
118	
119	// At booking: customer authorizes the block price.
120	priceForBlock(provider, blockMinutes) -> price_block_cents
121	
122	// At session end:
123	overageMinutes = max(0, ceil((elapsedSeconds - blockMinutes*60) / 60))
124	totalCents     = price_block_cents + overageMinutes * overage_per_min_cents
125	commissionCents      = round(totalCents * COMMISSION)
126	providerEarningsCents = totalCents - commissionCents   // + any tip added later
127	```
128	
129	Rules: round half-up to the nearest cent; a tip (from a review) is added to `provider_earnings_cents` and is **not** subject to commission; a no-show/early-cancel policy releases or partially captures the hold (define a simple rule: cancel ≥1h before scheduled = full release; in-progress end before block = still charge full block).
130	
131	---
132	
133	## 6. Screens & routes
134	
135	Follow `../Interactive_Prototype_Design_Brief.md` for visual + interaction detail. Route map (App Router):
136	
137	**Auth** — `/signin`, `/signup` (role chosen at sign-up: customer or provider).
138	
139	**Customer**
140	- `/` — Welcome (marketing).
141	- `/browse` — Discover listeners (filters: topic, language, available-now, price; voice-intro players).
142	- `/listeners/[id]` — Listener profile (voice intro, bio, topics, reviews, "Talk now" / "Schedule").
143	- `/book/[providerId]` — Choose block (15/30/45) + now/scheduled; price summary; mock payment → `authorizeHold`.
144	- `/session/[id]` — Pre-call (waiting room) → in-call mock screen (count-up timer, mute, captions, end).
145	- `/session/[id]/summary` — Post-call: rating + optional tip + receipt.
146	- `/account` — Customer's bookings/history.
147	
148	**Provider**
149	- `/provider/onboarding` — Audio-first, step-based: record voice intro (upload to Storage), topics, languages, prices, availability → initiate mock background check (status `pending`).
150	- `/provider/dashboard` — Big "Available now" toggle, upcoming sessions, weekly earnings, rating.
151	- `/provider/sessions` + `/provider/session/[id]` — Incoming request → accept → in-session (mirrors customer call screen) → summary.
152	
153	**Admin**
154	- `/admin/providers` — Approval queue: list `pending` providers, view details + voice intro, **Approve / Reject / Suspend** (sets `status` and `bg_check_status`).
155	
156	---
157	
158	## 7. Key flows (server actions)
159	
160	1. **Sign-up / role** → create `auth.users` + `profiles` row with chosen role; provider sign-up also creates a `providers` row (`status=pending`).
161	2. **Provider onboarding** → update `providers`, upload `voice_intro_path` to Storage, `backgroundCheck.initiate()` → `bg_check_status=pending`.
162	3. **Admin approval** → set `providers.status=approved`, `bg_check_status=clear` (or reject/suspend).
163	4. **Browse** → query `approved` providers with filters; signed URLs for voice intros.
164	5. **Booking** → validate slot/availability → create `booking` (`pending`) → `payments.authorizeHold(price_block)` → `booking.status=confirmed`, write `payments` row.
165	6. **Session start** → `calls.createSession()` → `session` (`in_progress`), `booking.status=in_progress`; render mock call; timer runs.
166	7. **Session end** → read elapsed → `pricing` computes overage/total/commission/earnings → `payments.capture(total)` → `recordProviderEarning()` → `session.status=completed`, `booking.status=completed` → route to summary.
167	8. **Review + tip** → create `review`, recompute `rating_avg`/`rating_count`, add tip to earnings.
168	9. **Weekly payouts (mock)** → `payments.runWeeklyPayouts()` aggregates per provider into `payouts`.
169	
170	Every action: Zod-validate input, check the caller's role/ownership, return typed result, handle errors gracefully.
171	
172	---
173	
174	## 8. Folder structure
175	
176	```
177	app/
178	  (marketing)/page.tsx                 # /
179	  (auth)/signin/  (auth)/signup/
180	  (customer)/browse/  listeners/[id]/  book/[providerId]/  session/[id]/  account/
181	  (provider)/provider/onboarding/  dashboard/  sessions/  session/[id]/
182	  (admin)/admin/providers/
183	  api/webhooks/payments/  api/webhooks/calls/   # for real adapters later
184	lib/
185	  integrations/{payments,calls,background-check}/{interface,mock,real,index}.ts
186	  supabase/{client,server,middleware}.ts
187	  db/queries.ts        validation/schemas.ts     pricing.ts     auth.ts
188	components/
189	  ui/                  # design-system primitives (Button, Field, Card, Dialog…)
190	  customer/  provider/ admin/  shared/
191	messages/en.json       # all user-facing copy (i18n-ready)
192	supabase/migrations/*.sql   supabase/seed.sql
193	tests/                 # unit + component + e2e
194	CLAUDE.md   BUILD_PLAN.md   README.md   .env.example
195	```
196	
197	---
198	
199	## 9. Configuration (`.env.example`)
200	
201	```
202	NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=
203	NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=
204	SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=
205	INTEGRATIONS_MODE=mock            # mock | real
206	PLATFORM_COMMISSION_RATE=0.05
207	NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_NAME=Heard
208	# Real integrations (later, unused in mock mode):
209	# STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=  STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET=  STRIPE_CONNECT_CLIENT_ID=
210	# ZOOM_MEETING_SDK_KEY=  ZOOM_MEETING_SDK_SECRET=  ZOOM_S2S_ACCOUNT_ID=  ZOOM_S2S_CLIENT_ID=  ZOOM_S2S_CLIENT_SECRET=
211	# CHECKR_API_KEY=
212	```
213	
214	---
215	
216	## 10. Accessibility (build-time requirements)
217	
218	Treat as acceptance criteria, not aspiration:
219	- Semantic HTML, one logical heading order, landmarks; real `<button>`/`<a>`.
220	- **Keyboard-operable everywhere**, visible focus ring on every interactive element (never remove without a stronger replacement).
221	- All controls labeled (`aria-label`/associated `<label>`); icon-only buttons forbidden.
222	- No state by color alone — pair with text/icon.
223	- Live-region announcements for state changes (availability on/off, "call connected — timer started", booking confirmed).
224	- Body text ≥ 18px; layout survives 200% zoom; contrast AA (AAA on body).
225	- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`; no autoplaying audio.
226	- Persistent "companionship, not therapy / crisis support" link on every page.
227	- Integrate **axe** checks into the component tests; a screen must pass before its milestone is "done".
228	
229	---
230	
231	## 11. Testing & quality
232	
233	- **Unit (Vitest):** `lib/pricing.ts` (blocks, overage, commission, tips, rounding), each mock adapter, validation schemas.
234	- **Component (React Testing Library + axe):** core screens render, are keyboard-navigable, and pass a11y checks.
235	- **E2E (Playwright):** two happy paths — (a) customer browse → book → run mock session → rate; (b) provider onboard → admin approve → appears in browse.
236	- **Types:** TypeScript `strict`. **Lint:** ESLint + Prettier. CI runs typecheck + lint + tests.
237	
238	---
239	
240	## 12. Explicitly out of scope (this build)
241	
242	Real Stripe/Zoom/Checkr calls (mock only); native mobile apps; on-demand matching algorithm; **moderation/reporting UI** (the `reports` table and an in-app "Report a problem" button that writes to it are included as a minimal safety hook, but no admin moderation screen yet); subscriptions; insurance/benefits payer model. These are noted as fast-follows; design the schema and adapters so none require a rewrite.
243	
244	---
245	
246	## 13. Definition of done (whole build)
247	
248	- All routes in §6 implemented and reachable; the customer and provider happy paths in §11 pass E2E.

1	# CLAUDE.md — "Heard"
2	
3	Conventions and guardrails for building this app. **Read `SPEC.md` for the full spec and `BUILD_PLAN.md` for the milestone order.** This file holds the rules you must follow on every change.
4	
5	## What this is
6	A two-sided marketplace where customers pay to talk with companion listeners who are all legally blind or visually impaired. Non-clinical companionship — **never** therapy. Accessibility and the dignity of providers are the whole point of the product.
7	
8	## Stack
9	Next.js (App Router) · TypeScript (`strict`) · Supabase (Postgres + Auth + Storage) · Tailwind CSS · Zod · Vitest + React Testing Library + Playwright · deploy to Vercel + Supabase.
10	
11	## Golden rules (do not violate)
12	1. **Accessibility is non-negotiable.** WCAG 2.2 AA minimum, AAA contrast on body text. Keyboard-operable, visible focus, semantic HTML, labeled controls, no state by color alone. A screen isn't done until it passes axe in tests. See `SPEC.md` §10.
13	2. **External services only through adapters.** Reach payments/calls/background-checks via `lib/integrations/*/index.ts` (`getPayments()`, `getCalls()`, `getBackgroundCheck()`). Never import `mock.ts`/`real.ts` directly; never call Stripe/Zoom/Checkr SDKs outside `real.ts`. Default mode is `mock`.
14	3. **All money is integer cents.** No floats for currency. All pricing/commission math lives in `lib/pricing.ts` and nowhere else. Commission comes from `PLATFORM_COMMISSION_RATE` (config), never a literal.
15	4. **Security: RLS on every table.** Customers/providers touch only their own rows; public reads only approved-provider public fields; admin sees all. The `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` is server-only — never shipped to the client, never in a client component.
16	5. **Validate at the boundary.** Every server action and route handler validates input with Zod and checks the caller's role/ownership before doing work.
17	6. **Server-first.** Prefer React Server Components + Server Actions; use client components only for genuinely interactive UI. No secrets in client bundles.
18	7. **All user-facing copy goes through `messages/en.json`** (i18n-ready) — no hard-coded strings in components.
19	8. **Safety framing in the product.** Every page carries the "companionship, not therapy — crisis support" affordance. Don't add anything that implies medical/mental-health treatment.
20	
21	## Conventions
22	- Components: PascalCase files; one component per file; design-system primitives in `components/ui` (Button, Field, Card, Dialog, …) used everywhere for consistent a11y.
23	- Styling: Tailwind core utilities + the design tokens from `../Interactive_Prototype_Design_Brief.md` (warm & trustworthy palette, 18px+ body, ≥48px tap targets).
24	- Data access: queries in `lib/db/queries.ts`; Zod schemas in `lib/validation/schemas.ts`.
25	- Errors: never swallow; return typed results and show friendly, accessible error states.
26	- Tests live in `tests/`; add/extend tests with every feature.
27	
28	## Commands
29	```
30	npm run dev            # local dev
31	npm run build          # production build
32	npm run lint           # eslint + prettier
33	npm run typecheck      # tsc --noEmit
34	npm run test           # vitest (unit + component)
35	npm run test:e2e       # playwright
36	supabase db reset      # apply migrations + seed (6 sample providers)
37	```
38	
39	## Definition of done (every feature/PR)
40	- TypeScript passes (`strict`), lint clean.
41	- Keyboard-navigable + axe a11y check passes for any new/changed screen.
42	- New logic has unit tests; pricing/accounting changes have explicit cases (blocks, overage, commission, tips, rounding).
43	- Inputs Zod-validated; RLS/ownership respected; no secrets client-side.
44	- User-facing strings in `messages/en.json`.
45	
46	## Out of scope right now
47	Real Stripe/Zoom/Checkr calls, moderation/reporting admin UI (table + minimal report hook only), native mobile, subscriptions. Keep schema/adapters ready so these don't need a rewrite. See `SPEC.md` §12.

findings.title: Nested Link>Button interactive elements (WCAG 2.5.1 violation)
findings.detail: Multiple screen-reader-visible issues: <Link><Button> nesting violates HTML spec. In app/(customer)/listeners/[id]/page.tsx (lines 82–84, 86–89) and app/(customer)/session/[id]/summary/page.tsx (lines 95–100), Button elements are wrapped inside Link elements. This creates a nested interactive region: the anchor role shadows the button, breaking semantic meaning and confusing AT users. Screen reader users will hear "link" but the focused element's role is button; keyboard focus and ARIA state announcements diverge.
findings.recommendation: Replace <Link><Button>text</Button></Link> with a single <Button as Link> wrapper (change Button to accept an `as` or `href` prop), or use a <Link> only and style it as a button without wrapping Button. Preserve the Button's label text and icon. This is a high-priority fix: nested interactives are a strong WCAG 2.1 fail.

findings.title: Dialog focus trap relies on native behavior; initial focus not set
findings.detail: components/ui/Dialog.tsx uses the native <dialog> element for focus trapping and Esc-to-close. The comment correctly notes these are 'free', but there is no explicit initial focus on the first focusable element (e.g., via autoFocus on the close button or a ref.current.focus() after showModal()). Keyboard users opening a dialog will find focus remains on the triggering element, not moved into the dialog. The Esc key works (native), but the first-Tab navigation and initial focus story are implicit. Screen readers may not announce the modal has opened clearly in all browsers without explicit focus management.
findings.recommendation: Add an autoFocus attribute to the close button (or a focusable element inside the dialog content) to move focus into the dialog on open. Alternatively, use a ref and call .focus() on the first focusable element in a useEffect after showModal() completes. This ensures keyboard and screen-reader users immediately know they are in a modal context.

findings.title: Session call screen lacks live region for captions; timer not announced by label
findings.detail: CallStage.tsx correctly has aria-live='polite' on the captions paragraph (line 91), which is good. However, the timer (line 81–87) has role='timer' and aria-label, but the label is static: 'Session timer' does not update with the current elapsed time. Screen readers will announce the label once; subsequent timer updates are visual only. The timer value (fmt(elapsed)) is not part of the aria-label, so each second's change is not announced. This means visually impaired listeners cannot track elapsed time via their screen reader without manually navigating back to the timer element.
findings.recommendation: Change the timer element to use aria-live='off' (or remove it) and instead announce timer milestones (e.g., every 5 minutes or at session-block boundaries) via the Toast announce() function. Alternatively, make the aria-label dynamic: include the current formatted time (e.g., aria-label={`Session timer: ${fmt(elapsed)}`}) and wrap the element in a live region. For the mock call, announce 'timer started' on connect (already done at line 55) and 'time remaining: X minutes' at key intervals.

findings.title: Mute and captions buttons lack clear visual state indication for color-blind users
findings.detail: CallStage.tsx buttons (lines 99–121) use aria-pressed and CSS :hover/:focus to signal state, which is correct. However, the pressed state for the captions button relies solely on bg-primary-tint / text-primary-dark (line 117), a color shift. The mute button (line 103) changes the icon (Mic vs MicOff) but the pressed state is subtle: only the background changes to surface-sunk with no text change. For color-blind users (especially common among the blind audience), the visual difference between pressed and unpressed may be unclear. Icons alone should not convey state (SPEC §10).
findings.recommendation: Pair the icon state change with a text label change inside the button (already present: 'mute'/'unmute' and 'captions on'/'captions off'), and ensure the background and text contrast meets WCAG AA even in the unpressed state. The icon + text is correct; verify via contrast checker that the hue shift (surface-sunk to primary-tint) is sufficient for color-blind users. Consider adding a subtle border or box-shadow change (not color alone) to reinforce state.

findings.title: No explicit navigation/header landmark; skip-link points to #main but main is in layout, not page
findings.detail: app/layout.tsx has a skip-link (line 39–44) that correctly points to #main with sr-only focus behavior. The #main id is present on the main element in every layout (layout.tsx shows examples). This is correct. However, there is no <nav> landmark for the site navigation. If navigation exists (e.g., AppHeader), it should be wrapped in <nav role='navigation'> or <nav aria-label='main'>, not a <div>. The skip-link will work for keyboard users, but the absence of a nav landmark means screen-reader users cannot jump directly to navigation with keyboard shortcuts.

findings.title: Reduced-motion: animations are respected, but the waveform is pure CSS (good)
findings.detail: app/globals.css (lines 174–182) correctly uses @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) to kill all animations. The waveform animations in VoicePlayer, CallStage, and SessionFlow all use CSS @keyframes wf (line 165), which will be disabled under reduced-motion. This is correct. However, there is no visual fallback state documented: under reduced-motion, the bars are static at 0.4 scale (line 166 default), which is visually thin. Screen-reader users already ignore the waveform (aria-hidden), so this is acceptable, but low-vision users under reduced-motion may find the static bars unclear. Minor polish only.

findings.title: Contrast verified in theme tokens; 'accent-strong' and 'success-strong' ensure AA on tints

Button text is always --color-surface on darker backgrounds (primary, amber, alert), which are explicitly designed for WCAG AA+. The design system is sound. However, no actual contrast ratio measurements were provided in the CSS comments; the claim '≥4.5:1' is asserted but not validated. StatusBadge uses these pairings correctly (components/ui/StatusBadge.tsx, lines 8–14).
findings.recommendation: Add a comment with measured contrast ratios for key pairings (e.g., --color-ink on --color-bg, --color-accent-strong on --color-accent-tint) to document compliance. This is already implemented correctly; a measurement doc is a polish for maintenance. No code change needed.

findings.title: Form error association and required state correct in Field wrapper
findings.detail: components/ui/Field.tsx (lines 30–72) correctly wires error messages via aria-describedby and sets aria-invalid=true when an error is present (line 62). aria-required is set when required=true (line 63). Input elements inherit these attributes via the children render prop (lines 59–64). This is correct and well-structured. The error is also marked with role='alert' (line 66) so screen readers announce it immediately. However, the pattern relies on the Input component receiving the props correctly; there is no test that verifies end-to-end error announcement in a form (e.g., submit → error → alert announced). The unit tests for components pass axe, but no form submission scenario explicitly tests error handling announcement.

Optional: add an e2e or component test scenario that submits a form with an invalid field, verifies the error message is present and announced via role='alert', and that focus remains on the field. This would be a good test addition (not a bug fix).

findings.title: No test coverage for 200% zoom / reflow scenario
findings.detail: SPEC §10 requires 'layout survives 200% zoom; contrast AA (AAA on body)'. The test suite (Vitest + Playwright) does not include a zoom/reflow scenario. ## Accessibility Audit Summary

I have completed a thorough accessibility audit of the Heard application against WCAG 2.2 AA standards. Here are the findings organized by severity:

### Critical Issues (High Severity - Risk)

**1. Nested Link>Button Interactive Elements**
- **Location**: `/app/(customer)/listeners/[id]/page.tsx` (lines 82–89) and `/app/(customer)/session/[id]/summary/page.tsx` (lines 95–100)
- **Problem**: Multiple instances wrap `<Button>` inside `<Link>`, creating nested interactive regions. Screen readers report the element as a link, but the actual DOM node is a button, causing semantic confusion. This violates HTML spec and WCAG 2.5.1 (target size / nested interactives).
- **Fix**: Replace with either a single styled `<Link>` (styled as a button) or change the `Button` component to accept an `as` prop to render as a link when needed.

### Important Gaps (Medium Severity - Partial Implementation)

**2. Dialog Focus Management**
- **Location**: `/components/ui/Dialog.tsx`
- **Problem**: While using the native `<dialog>` element is excellent, there is no explicit initial focus management. When a dialog opens, focus should move to the first focusable element inside (usually the close button), but currently it remains on the trigger element.
- **Fix**: Add `autoFocus` to the close button or use a ref with `focus()` in a useEffect to move focus into the dialog on open.

**3. Timer on Live Call Not Announced**
- **Location**: `/components/session/CallStage.tsx` (lines 81–87)
- **Problem**: The timer has `role="timer"` and a static `aria-label`, but the label doesn't update with the elapsed time. Each second, the visual timer changes but screen-reader users hear nothing new. They must manually navigate back to read the timer value.
- **Fix**: Either announce time milestones (every 5 minutes) via the Toast `announce()` function, or make the `aria-label` dynamic to include the current time.

**4. Captions and Mute State Indication**
- **Location**: `/components/session/CallStage.tsx` (lines 99–121)
- **Problem**: The muted and captions button states rely on icon changes and subtle background color shifts. For color-blind users, the visual state difference may be unclear.
- **Fix**: Ensure the text labels inside buttons clearly change state ('Mute'/'Unmute', 'Captions On'/'Captions Off') and pair with sufficient contrast/visual change for color-blind accessibility.

**5. No Navigation Landmark**
- **Location**: `/components/shared/AppHeader.tsx` (if navigation exists)
- **Problem**: No explicit `<nav>` landmark found. Screen-reader users cannot use keyboard shortcuts to jump to navigation.
- **Fix**: Wrap site navigation in a `<nav>` element with an appropriate `aria-label`.

### Test Coverage Gaps (Medium Severity)

**6. No 200% Zoom / Reflow Test Coverage**
- **Location**: Test suite (Vitest + Playwright)
- **Problem**: SPEC §10 requires layout to survive 200% zoom. The test suite does not verify this scenario.
- **Fix**: Add a Playwright e2e test that loads key screens at 200% zoom and verifies no horizontal scrolling and no cut-off content.

### Minor Issues & Observations (Low Severity - Polish)

- **Reduced-Motion**: Correctly implemented in globals.css; animations disable under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- **Contrast Tokens**: Design system tokens are sound (`--color-accent-strong` on `--color-accent-tint` = ≥4.5:1), but actual ratio measurements are not documented in comments.
- **Icon-Only Controls**: Checked. `Button` component enforces text labels. Toggle buttons (heart, play) use `aria-label`, which is compliant.
- **Form Errors**: Correctly wired via `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid`, and `role="alert"`. No test gap here.
- **Heading Order**: Clean, single h1 per page, correct hierarchy.
- **Focus Rings**: Universal blue outline at 3px via focus-visible; correct throughout.
- **Safety Banner & Crisis Resources**: Exemplary implementation; persistent, accessible, clear.
- **Live Regions**: Toast system (aria-live polite/assertive) is well-designed. Session connection announcement is correct.

### Summary

The Heard codebase demonstrates strong accessibility foundations: semantic HTML, keyboard navigation, visible focus rings, form labels, live regions, and a thoughtful design system. However, three structural issues need urgent attention: the nested Link/Button pattern, dialog initial focus, and timer announcement. The test coverage should be expanded to include 200% zoom validation. With these fixes, the application will meet WCAG 2.2 AA standards comprehensively and honor the core promise that accessibility is "the whole point of the product."
